Alliance 1–30 Field Guide

Four starting paths, one merge point. Hub-by-hub routes for Humans, Dwarves and Gnomes, Night Elves and Alliance Skyborne, with what Forever changed, when to run each dungeon, and which professions to pick up where.

Launch day: the first two hours

What to do before the servers open at 10 am Thursday, and a checklist for your first two hours in each starting zone.

World of Warcraft: Forever launches
Thursday 5 November, 10:00 am AEDT (Wed 4 Nov 3:00 pm PST · 23:00 UTC · one global time) Official

Before 10 am

  1. Install the live client. In the Battle.net app pick World of Warcraft, then World of Warcraft: Forever in the Game Version menu (not the beta) and install. It's already out, so do it the night before.
  2. Pick your ruleset. There are no realms: you choose Normal, PvP, Roleplaying or Roleplay-PvP, and each is one big shared world. Oceanic players connect to Australian servers, and your chat language decides who shares your world. A PvP account is locked to one faction.
  3. Install the seven addons. OneForAll first, then the rest of the must-haves in the Addons tab. Forever uses the modern client, so Classic Era builds won't load.
  4. Set up your character here. Pick race and class in Your character so the guide folds away the other routes and marks your weapons, armour and professions.
  5. Be online before 10:00. Blizzard has published no queue estimate. Beta day one had queues of 17,000 to 22,000 (up to about 48 minutes). Reserved names get no head start: everyone starts at level 1. Unverified
  6. Group before boats and cities. Layering stays. Accepting a party invite moves you to the leader's layer, so form your group before a boat or zeppelin and check it after entering a capital.

Changed, and will catch you out

  • Bags no longer equip themselves: drag every new bag into a bag slot.
  • New spells don't go on your bars: drag them from the spellbook after every trainer visit.
  • Respawns are faster for launch, fastest in the starter zones, and Blizzard will wind them back once the rush passes.
  • Training every class spell from 1 to 60 now costs about 206 g, whatever your class.
  • Camp buffs need a full minute seated at the fire. A datamine of the 30 Oct build shows the Adventurer's Tent shrinking to a 15-minute miniature tent, so don't plan your rest around it.

From Blizzard's 2 Nov development notes, apart from the tent datamine. Official

What Forever changed for 1–30

Nine things that make a 2019 Classic route misleading, and what to do instead.

Dungeons: once for the quests, then leave Official

Dungeon kill XP sits far below Classic (beta measurements put Deadmines trash at roughly a quarter of the old value) while dungeon quest XP is boosted, trimmed to about 2.4× Classic in the 1 Oct build. Blizzard's stated goal: one or two runs per dungeon should keep pace with the best questing route, and dungeon-grinding should not beat it. Mage AoE boosting is intentionally weak.

Quest XP is the engine Official

Total XP to 60 is unchanged (about 4.08 million). Over 1,000 new quests were added across 1–60, so hubs are denser than the 2019 spreadsheet suggests. Treat Classic quest levels as a map, then follow what the Forever client actually offers.

New ship: Stormwind Harbor ↔ Auberdine Verified in beta

A direct boat links Stormwind Harbor and Darkshore. Night Elves can join the Westfall → Deadmines line at 10–12, and Humans can reach Blackfathom Deeps without the Wetlands run. A one-way Menethil → Southshore → Auberdine → Menethil loop also exists.

Rested stacks with food and camps Official

Rested XP doubles kill XP (5% of a level per 8 h in an inn or city, cap 150%). Most cooked food gives Well Fed (check the tooltip says so), which adds +5% kill XP. From level 14 the Cozy Sleeping Bag adds up to +3% and counts as an inn for rest. A Leatherworking Camp Tent tops up rested XP by 5% of a level once an hour.

Camping is a system now Official

Cooking 1 turns a cooking fire into a Basic Campfire. Sit at it for a minute to take camp buffs; profession camp items unlock at skill 20 (First Aid Kit for Stamina, Herbalism candle for Intellect, Skinning chair for crit, and so on). All share a 1-hour cooldown. The Great Outdoors quest (level 4+) teaches it in every Alliance start: Sam Sarsaparilla (Goldshire), Eric Brighthammer (Kharanos), Lyreena Duskblade (Dolanaar) and Raan Wildwind (Shen'dar).

Legacy points help every alt Verified in beta

Account-wide challenges replace achievements. First point: any character to level 25, or 150 in a crafting skill. Useful ranks: Well Rested (rested accrues faster), Talented (first talent point at 9), Thrill of Adventure (kills restore 1% HP/mana), Frequent Flier (half-price flights).

Group XP fixed Official

Each party member's XP now follows their own level even with a higher-level member present (8 Oct fix). Enemies far below someone's level give that player nothing, so keep groups within a few levels. Five players split kill XP ÷5 then ×1.4; quest turn-ins are unaffected.

Addon limits Verified in beta

Forever runs on the modern client with Midnight-era restrictions: addons cannot read the combat log, and in-combat aura and cooldown values are hidden. WeakAuras has no Forever build (ForeverAuras and Musca Auras are forks). Questie has an official Forever build from v12.0.1.

New race and class combinations

Alliance gains Human Hunter, Dwarf Shaman and Gnome Priest. There are no new Night Elf combinations. Skyborne can be Druid, Hunter, Rogue or Warrior on either side, plus Mage on the Alliance (High Order) side only. All weapon-skill racials are gone and Hit is a single stat for spells and attacks. The 2 Nov launch patch: what touches 1–30

Blizzard's last pre-launch patch (2 Nov, applied for the 4 Nov launch) is mostly class tuning for level 60. These are the parts that change how you level. Official

ChangeWhat to do about it
Spawn rates raised for launch. Starter zones respawn fastest, higher zones less so, and Blizzard will wind the starter-zone boost back after the rushCamps that were a slog in beta (Ursera bears on Zephras, the Kobold mines) should move quickly in week one. Expect copper, herbs and leather to flood the auction house faster too
Bags no longer auto-equip. A new bag goes into your pack, not an empty slotDrag it to a bag slot. If a bag quest reward 'didn't work', check your pack
New spells no longer land on your action bars.After every trainer visit, open the spellbook and drag the new rank out. Easy to miss a rank-2 Fireball or Rend
Training costs equalised: about 206–207 g for every spell from 1 to 60, whatever the class. Same-level abilities cost the sameBudget the same way for any class. Still skip spells you don't use; Dual Spec and riding wait until 40
Quest XP rewards adjusted, and more quests had their prerequisites and level requirements fixedThe zone XP totals in this guide come from beta; expect small shifts. Follow the chapter order, not the exact numbers
Satyrs are now Demons, not HumanoidsAshenvale satyr camps (Satyrnaar, Felfire Hill, Zoram Strand Fallenroot): Warlocks can Banish and Enslave them, and Paladins' Exorcism and the new Turn Evil talent work on them. Rogue Sap, humanoid-only in Classic, likely no longer does
Class milestones moved. Paladin Righteous Fury at 10 (was 16). Rogue Shank at 24 (off-hand attack, generates energy) and Poised at 18. Druid Ferocious Bite gains a rank at 24; Lacerate is now a Feral talent. Dwarf Shaman: Improved Ghost Wolf moved to row 4Noted in the level checklist. Shaman levellers can't get instant Ghost Wolf early any more
Hunter traps share one 30 s cooldown; Aimed, Arcane and Serpent Sting hit much harderFreezing Trap and Immolation Trap no longer both. Pick one per pull in the Deadmines and Stockade
Warlock pets scale far less with your Stamina (2 HP per point, was 7.5). Shadow Word: Death backlash is 30% of max HP if the target survives (was 10%)Voidwalker tanks need more Health Funnel and a bandage habit at 20+. Priests: finish with Death only on a sure kill
Damage up across most classes, with enemy health raised at higher levels to compensate. Tank threat up: Defensive Stance 80%, Bear Form 115%, Righteous Fury 33% + 90% HolyDungeons at 1–30 should feel steadier for any tank
Downranking is back. Low-rank spells no longer have a reduced chance to trigger talents (the October beta had cut it to 0% for very old ranks). The one exception is Blizzard: a rank learned more than about 12 levels below yours still procs Arcane Concentration, Frostbite and Fingers of Frost less often. Frost Blast, the stop-gap cheap slow, is removedCasters: Rank 1 Frostbolt is a cheap slow that can still Frostbite; Rank 1 Lightning Bolt and Wrath fish for Clearcasting and Omen of Clarity again. Healers: at 1–30 every rank still carries nearly all of your +healing (the gear-bonus fade only bites 18 levels after a rank is learned), so heal with the rank that doesn't overheal. Drag the old ranks back onto your bars; new ranks don't replace them

Full notes: Blizzard forums, 2 Nov 2026. Blizzard says no major tuning is likely before raids open (9 Dec).

Dual Spec unlocks at level 40 (confirmed; 10 g or 50 g depending on the source). Riding is also at 40: 100 g training, and sources disagree on whether the first mount is included or costs about 20 g more. Neither touches 1–30, so spend nothing on it yet and bank the gold.

The route

Four paths, one merge

Where each race is at every level, and the shape of the whole trip.

The shape of 1–30

  • 1–10/12 stays in your starting zone. Every Alliance start now has a 6-slot bag quest or satchel reward early; take it (and equip it by hand).
  • 10–18 is one zone plus one dungeon run: Westfall + Deadmines, Loch Modan + Hall of Thanes, or Darkshore alone.
  • 18–22 is Redridge for three of the four paths; Night Elves stay in Kalimdor and use Stonetalon as the bridge.
  • 22–30 is Duskwood (with Wetlands for the dwarf line) or Ashenvale, with Blackfathom Deeps or the Excavation Site as the one dungeon worth a trip.

What to do at every level

  • 5 Apprentice professions. 6–7 first hearth move. 9 first talent point if you own the Legacy perk, else 10.
  • 10 City trip: class quest, Journeyman professions, bank, auction house. Set a bag goal: four 6-slot bags by 12, four 8–10 slot bags by 20. Since the 2 Nov patch new bags no longer equip themselves: drag them into a bag slot.
  • 14 Cozy Sleeping Bag chain starts (Westfall, 37, 50).
  • 20 Expert professions, second city trip, mage portals to Stormwind and Ironforge. 25 your first Legacy point.
  • 30 Beta's cap; Druid Travel Form, Warrior Berserker Rage. Nothing to buy for riding until 40.
Kill XP

What to kill at your level

Every kill is worth a fixed amount set by your level and the mob's level. A mob at your level is the yardstick: it gives 45 + 5 × your level, so 95 XP at level 10, 145 at 20 and 195 at 30. A mob above you is worth 5% more for each level it's higher, up to four levels (orange); red mobs give no more than orange. A mob below you loses a fixed slice for every level it's under, set by a number for your level bracket called the zero difference (ZD): each level below takes away one ZD-th of the kill, and at the grey level and below a kill gives nothing. Forever adds a second cut that Classic didn't have: for lower mobs it works out the base from the mob's level instead of yours, so a level-18 mob gives a level-20 character 110 XP where Classic gave 119. Blizzard has said this is intended, not a bug Verified in beta. So same level isn't the most per kill (a mob two levels up gives about 10% more) but it is usually the most per minute: higher mobs take longer, and more of your attacks miss and spells get resisted. Below your level, the value falls fast. In Forever a mob two levels below you is worth about two-thirds of a same-level kill at levels 10–15, three-quarters at 20 and four-fifths at 30.

Same level
XP = 45 + 5 × L
Higher, up to +4
XP = (45 + 5 × L) × (1 + 0.05 × levels above)Classic rule; not yet measured in Forever
Lower, above grey (Forever)
XP = (45 + 5 × M) × (1 − levels below ÷ ZD)Classic used L here, not M
Grey level (no XP at or below)
none before 6 · then L − ⌊L ÷ 10⌋ − 5at 6–39; level 10 → 4, 20 → 13, 30 → 22

L = your level, M = the mob's level. ZD by your level: 1–7 → 5 · 8–9 → 6 · 10–11 → 7 · 12–15 → 8 · 16–19 → 9 · 20–29 → 11 · 30–39 → 12. Results round to the nearest whole XP.

Your levelMob +2+1Same level−1−2−3−5
10ZD 7 · grey ≤ 4105110%100105%95100%7781% · Classic 816164% · Classic 684648% · Classic 542021% · Classic 27
20ZD 11 · grey ≤ 13160110%152105%145100%12788% · Classic 13211076% · Classic 1199565% · Classic 1056545% · Classic 79
30ZD 12 · grey ≤ 22215110%205105%195100%17489% · Classic 17915479% · Classic 16313569% · Classic 1469951% · Classic 114

Each cell: Forever XP for one solo kill, then its share of a same-level kill. Where Classic paid more, its figure follows. Higher-level columns use the Classic rule.

What this means in practice

  • Yellow mobs (within two levels of yours) are the sweet spot for questing: full or near-full value and quick kills. Your own level or one below is the best XP per minute for most classes.
  • Green mobs three or more levels below are mostly a waste unless they're a quest target. At 20, a level-15 mob gives 65 XP against 145 for a level-20 one.
  • Orange mobs pay up to +20% but cost more time and potions. Take them when they're quest targets, not to farm.
  • When everything around you turns green, it's time to move on. That's what the level bands in each zone chapter are for.

What multiplies a kill

  • Elite mobs give 2× (and a group shares it).
  • Rested doubles kill XP until your rested pool runs out; quest turn-ins aren't doubled.
  • Well Fed from most cooked food adds +5% kill XP (the tooltip must say Well Fed), and the Cozy Sleeping Bag adds up to +3%.
  • Dungeon mobs give far less than in Classic in Forever: players measured about 70% below Classic even after the 8 Oct +20% buff. Run dungeons for the quests.

Hearth discipline beats every other trick. Bind at the hub you will return to most in the next 3–5 levels, not the nicest inn, and log out in it. Rested XP is the single largest multiplier you control.

Start here

Rest and camping planner

How much rest tonight's log-out earns, where to log out on your route, an hour at camp, and the food worth carrying for the +5%.

Rest is the biggest XP multiplier you control. In an inn or a capital, rest builds at 5% of your level per 8 hours, logged in or out, up to 150% of a level (about 10 days from empty). It doubles kill XP until the pool runs out; quest turn-ins aren't doubled and don't use it. Forever adds three things on top: the Leatherworking Camp Tent, the Cozy Sleeping Bag (a rest area you carry, from level 14), and the Well Rested Legacy perk (+4% rest rate and cap per rank, 5 ranks). Verified in beta

Tonight's log-out

Open-world rest at a quarter of the inn rate is Classic behaviour; no Forever source has confirmed it Classic data. With Well Rested the cap rise may be 150% → 180% or → 170%; the planner uses the smaller.

An hour at camp

  1. 0:00Drop a Basic Campfire Kit (Cooking 1: 1 Simple Wood with Flint and Tinder). It burns about 10 minutes and holds up to 3 features from different players.
  2. 0:00Each player places one camp feature (Camp Tent, Chair, Candle, First Aid Kit and so on). Placing any one starts a shared 1-hour cooldown on all of yours.
  3. 0:01Sit or craft at the fire for a full minute: every feature's buff applies and lasts an hour. They don't stack with the matching class buff.
  4. 0:01Leatherworker's Camp Tent: tops your stored rest up to 5% of a level if you have less. Boosted Rest then locks it for an hour.
  5. 0:02Eat while seated: most cooked food gives Well Fed, +5% kill XP for 15 minutes (about 30 with the Gourmand perk). Re-eat every quarter hour.
  6. 0:03From level 14, unroll the Cozy Sleeping Bag and lie on it for 3 minutes: +1% XP per minute up to +3%. It shares nothing with the camp cooldowns. Verified in beta
  7. 1:00Cooldowns are back: relight, replace, re-sit. Field Guide (Legacy) trims the camp cooldown by 8%; Permanence makes camp buffs last 50% longer. Verified in beta

Which object each profession makes, and what it buffs, is in Professions → Camping objects.

Leave at 15–18. From here the efficient line is: Tram to Stormwind → Deadmines with every quest in the log (17–19) → Westfall clean-up → Redridge (19–21) → Wetlands (21–25) → Duskwood (25–30). See the Human chapters for Westfall, Redridge and Duskwood.

Chapter 4

Skyborne: Zephras Isle

The new race's floating 1–12 island, and how to get from it to Westfall.

Skyborne · Levels 1–12

A floating island in Skywall, shared by both factions but phased so you only see your own side's quests. The isle is U-shaped and vertical: learn Walk on Air in the first batch of quests and glide between hubs instead of walking the switchbacks. Hub order runs north to south down the western arm, then into Valanaar at the south-east tip, then back up the eastern arm for the finale. Verified in beta

1

Thendal Village 42, 23 1–5

Start. Rorian the Dayseeker and Aetheen of the Gales run the chain; class trainers here teach to level 6.
  1. 1Coming of Age → Harmony in Balance (8 Vuldren Juveniles; opens your L2 class quest)
  2. 2Infestation Investigation (8 Pesky Cirrusflies) → The Cirrusfly Queen
  3. 2Falling With Style (teaches Walk on Air) · The Anchors of Zephras (Halaan Hawk-Eye)
  4. 3Elemental Unrest → Agitators (6 Rolling Winds, 7 Al'Aketh Converts in the northern valley)
  5. 4Harvesting Windstones (rewards a gathering-profession voucher) · Reading the Ley Lines (teaches Read Leyline) · Aggressive Encroachment (Valreaa Valewind)
  6. 4Return to Rorian → Aetheen of the Gales
  7. 5Foul Matriarch (Thendal Cave) → The Next Step

Foul Matriarch / Head of Urs'anah is the hardest starting-zone quest in the game so far: the Ursera bears are packed tight, respawn fast (faster still with the launch spawn boost) and swarm from behind. Pull one at a time from the cave mouth or take a partner. Reward includes a choice of Worn Greatsword, Novice's Quarterstaff, Scout Ranger's Dagger, Peacekeeper's Pickhammer or Refined Shortbow.

The Agitators valley has wide social aggro. Work the edges and let Converts come to you.

Vulgara's hill cannot be jumped; walk in from the north. Soloable around level 7 for most classes with a potion ready.

Pick up Apprentice gathering here and spend the Windstone voucher. Herbalism: Halassa Fernbreeze (43.0, 43.6). Mining: Messana Crestwind (44.8, 44.4). First Aid: Naleeia Tattermend (43.0, 46.2). Alchemy and Cooking are next door (43.8, 43.6–43.8).

Sanctum of Storms (finale) — 11–12

  1. 11Tower Defense · Disrupting Logistics · Breaking the Breaker → Return to Valanaar
  2. 12The High Elder's Request → The Turncoat → Al'Aketh Assassins → The Cult's True Plans → Desperate Times → Prepare for Battle → Making Our Move → The Inner Sanctum → Confront Lorthuna
  3. 12Kirin Tor and Earthen Ring reinforcements open a portal; report to your faction leader, then take “The Magical City of Dalaran” from Elaadrin Evengale

Beta players often leave at 10 because the second half slows down; a full clear lands at 13–14. If you have a Westfall route waiting, leaving after Gustberry (≈11) is the efficient call.

Blessing of Zephras: touch the small tornadoes for +40% move speed. It only drops when you attack something, so keep it while running between hubs. Windstones are isle-only potions; use them freely, they don't travel.

Leaving the isle (Alliance)

Take the eastern Skydock 65.9, 83.5 (boats every ~5 minutes; either faction can ride either boat). You land on a balcony on Dalaran's north side, in the Alterac Mountains. Hand in to Denaaris Stargale in the Sky Enclave, take “Welcome to Azeroth”, then use the portal to Stormwind in the portal room opposite the dock. It exits at the Stormwind Mage Tower. “Exploring the Alliance” then tours Stormwind, Ironforge and Darnassus and points you at Westfall. Verified in beta

Your hearth stays bound to the isle until you re-bind, so set it in Stormwind (or Goldshire) before you leave the city. Dalaran holds the City of Dalaran dungeon (Alliance quests from 30) and sits beside Hillsbrad and Alterac, whose Alliance quests run 30–40: too high at 12, the next stop at 30. You can leave the isle at any level and come back by the same boat.

Chapter 5

Levels 30–40: the next chapter

Where the Alliance goes after the merge: Southshore and Dalaran, Arathi, Stranglethorn, Alterac, then Desolace, Dustwallow or the new Riverglades.

Nobody has played this route in Forever: the beta stopped at level 30 and the cap was never lifted. Everything here is Classic quest data plus Forever client data, with the new Forever quests added where they are known. Expect the first week after launch to correct things, and treat coordinates as Classic positions.

Forever guides agree on the 30–35 core: Arathi Highlands, Stranglethorn Vale, Desolace and Alterac Mountains, with Hillsbrad (Southshore) carried over from the late 20s. Warcraft Tavern lists Alterac, Arathi, Desolace and Stranglethorn as its level-30 zones. Verified in beta

For 35–40+ the same guides name Dustwallow Marsh, Badlands, Swamp of Sorrows and the new Riverglades (Feralas also appears at 35 in Warcraft Tavern's list). Thousand Needles shows up only in Conquest Capped's 30–40 list and as Horde 25–35 in WoW Forever Guides. Verified in beta

The suggested line

LevelsWhereWhy
30Southshore and the City of Dalaran questsThe new breadcrumb from Stormwind lands you here at 30; An Alarming Request (level 30) gets the Dalaran sewer key, and Heart of Disruption alone is 9,400 XP.
31–35Arathi Highlands from Refuge PointeEvery Forever guide names it for 30–35. Come back at 38–40 for Faldir's Cove and the Circles of Binding.
33–37Stranglethorn Vale: Rebel Camp, Nesingwary, Booty BayThe densest quest zone of the band. Contested: expect world PvP around Grom'gol.
36–38Back to Southshore for AlteracStrahnbrad and the Syndicate, the Crushridge ogres, and the Warrior and Dwarf Shaman finales at Bath'rah.

36–40Riverglades (new)150+ new quests and a flight point with direct flights to Lakeshire and Thelsamar, but nothing about it was playable in beta. Likely the best 36–40 zone once launch players confirm it.

The zone picks match Conquest Capped, Warcraft Tavern and WoW Forever Guides; the order is ours. Unverified

Rebel Camp and Nesingwary's in the north are the 32–37 core; Booty Bay holds the rest and a second pass at 37–45 (Bloodsail, Mistvale, Zanzil). Forever adds new quests around Booty Bay and the Kurzen camps (Zimmix's Great Escape, The Cook in the Cage, Returning to Port, Talk of the Town, Reduce, Reuse, Reconcile) and the new Drowned City dungeon off the north-west coast. Zone area levels 30–44; contested. Classic data

No Alliance flight point or town. Every Alliance quest here is handed out in Southshore, so Alterac is a set of trips north from Southshore at 34–40: Syndicate at Strahnbrad, Crushridge ogres, Baron Vardus. Forever redraws Dalaran in full (the shield is gone), adds the Old Dalaran Ruins and The Eventide, a new Kirin Tor reputation and one new quest, Strahnbrad Mystery. Zone area levels 27–39. Nijel's Point in the north holds most Alliance quests: satyrs at Sargeron, the Burning Blade at Thunder Axe Fortress, then kodos, goblins and centaurs to the south. Forever adds the most new content of any 30–40 zone here: Carved Centaur Totems drop from every centaur clan and buy rep and recipes from new quartermasters, and around twenty new quests (centaur khans, profession tasks, Vahlarriel's Vengeance). The Valley of Bones in the south is now part of the new Shen'dralas zone. Zone area levels 30–39. Classic data

Once you have found Nijel's Point, it links to Auberdine, Stonetalon Peak, Theramore and Feathermoon.

Forever's largest new zone, in south-east Khaz Modan between Redridge, Burning Steppes, Badlands and Swamp of Sorrows. Blizzard puts it across the mid-30s to mid-40s with more than 150 new quests. The Brotherhood of the Horse holds Farholde Keep for the Alliance; Twilight's Hammer occupies Sunnyglade; ogres hold the roads. Quest text, map and most of the dungeon were encrypted in beta files, so nobody has a route yet. Optional until launch reports confirm it beats Desolace or Dustwallow. Unverified

1

Farholde Keep 38

Alliance flight point. Routes in client data: Lakeshire 6 s 30 c, Thelsamar 6 s 30 c, Morgan's Vigil 6 s 30 c, Powderfuse Port 3 s 30 c. Ruler: Demar Brant. By land, a new fork off the Redridge road toward Burning Steppes; Redridge's east edge and new passes from Badlands also lead in.

Area levels: Meadowsbrook, Wheeler's Grange, Southern Watch 36 · Bristle Hills 37 · Farholde Keep, Elbrim's Farm, Sunnyglade, Terral's Watch, Turner's Logging Camp, Ashwood's Fall, Powderfuse Port 38 · Eastwind Shore 40 · Windstead 41 · Krol'dok Stronghold 42 · Twilight's Shroud, Forlorn Pit 44.

2

Powderfuse Port 38

Neutral goblin harbour (Powderfuse reputation, Steamwheedle Cartel). Boat to Steamwheedle Port, Tanaris. Client data shows an Alliance flight master with one route, to Farholde Keep (an unconfirmed beta forum post said there was no flight path).

Beta data: Krix teaches Apprentice and Journeyman Fishing; Grungle is a Mining trainer; Mister Graphed is an unlimited reagent vendor.

Coral Shark (elite 46–47) patrols nearby water.

Krol'dok Stronghold (40–45) is an ogre stronghold in the middle of the zone; only its last boss, Overlord Mugg, is known.

From Lakeshire or Thelsamar it's a short flight once you've walked in and taken the Farholde point.

Prospector Ryedol's Explorers' League camp starts the Uldaman storyline; most quests are 37–44, so this is the hand-off zone from the end of this chapter into the 40s. Level-by-level checklist

One line per level band: what to train, where to bind, which dungeon to run, which chain to start. Pair it with the zone chapters.

1
  • Junior gathering trainer + 4-slot pack; free gathering manual from the first starter quest
  • Humans: Hunter letter from Marshal McBride. Dwarf Shaman: Archaic Rune → Teo Hammerstorm
  • Skyborne: learn Walk on Air in the first batch
4–5
  • Crafting Apprentice (level 5), Cooking, First Aid, Fishing
  • The Great Outdoors (camping) at your starter town
  • Dwarf Shaman: Call of Earth totem quest
  • Bag quests: Grund and Gozwin (Dun Morogh), Book Return (Elwynn), Soft Saber Pelts for the 6-slot Soft Saber Sack (Aldia, Dolanaar), Prideclaws satchel (Zephras)
6–7
  • First hearth move: Goldshire → stays; Kharanos; Dolanaar; Shen'dar
  • Turn in collection quests (Zenn's Bidding at 7, not before)
9–10
  • First talent point (9 with the Legacy Talented perk, else 10)
  • City trip: class quest, Journeyman professions at skill 50, bank, auction house. Fly, tram or portal. Paladins: Righteous Fury now at 10. New spells don't appear on your bars: drag them from the spellbook
  • Camp object at skill 20 (from the Camping 101 quest for your profession)
  • Hunters: Taming the Beast ×3. Druids: Moonglade and Body and Heart. Shaman: Fire totem chain starts
  • Waylaid Crates open: your first sealed crate (or first Craftsman's Writ) gives a Shipping Label for 50 Favor, 2,000 Commerce Authority rep and 660 XP. Crates planner
11–12
  • Leave the starting zone with the breadcrumb in hand: Report to Gryan Stoutmantle · Stout to Kadrell · Flight to Auberdine · The Magical City of Dalaran
  • Take the first field flight point (Sentinel Hill, Thelsamar, Auberdine) and re-bind there
13–14
  • Hall of Thanes once (dwarf line) with the Farsen chain and three dungeon quests
  • Level 14: Cozy Sleeping Bag step 1 at the burned-out cart, Alexston Farmstead, Westfall 37.1, 50.1 (hand in at the Barrens)
  • Pre-collect Deadmines quests in the Stormwind Dwarven District
16–18
  • Redridge entry; The Defias Brotherhood's Lakeshire and Stormwind legs
  • Deadmines once at 18–20 with all quests; VanCleef's Unsent Letter opens the Stockade chain
  • Night Elves: Tower of Althalaxx (3) done, Trek to Ashenvale in the log
20
  • Expert professions at skill 125 in a city; Expert Cookbook and First Aid book
  • Mage portals to Stormwind and Ironforge. Druid Cat Form. Shaman Ghost Wolf and the Water totem chain. Rogues: Poised at 18, Shank at 24
  • Expert Waylaid Crates. Second hearth move: Lakeshire · Menethil · Astranaar
22–24
  • Stockade once at 24–26 with six quests, training in Stormwind on the same trip (Rogue Shank and Druid Ferocious Bite rank 2 at 24)
  • Night Elves: Blackfathom Deeps at 24–26 with five quests; one Stonetalon trip at 21–22
  • Dwarf line: Wetlands 21–25 with the new dungeon quests in the log
25
  • First Legacy point: spend it on Well Rested or Talented
  • Hearth to Darkshire; Raven Hill and Abercrombie chain
26–28
  • Excavation Site: Wetlands once (Songblade, Thicket Things, Highland Hides, Horrors, Lost Relic Carry → Heavehammer)
  • Ashenvale east side; Felfire Hill at 28+
29–30
  • Bank the elites for one grouped evening: Mor'Ladim, Morbent Fel, Stalvan, Bride of the Embalmer / Stitches, Ran Bloodtooth
  • Druid Travel Form, Warrior Berserker Rage. Nothing to spend on riding until 40
  • Line up Southshore and the City of Dalaran (from 30), then Arathi and Stranglethorn: Levels 30–40

Dungeon guide

Dungeons 1–30

Six instances, the levels to run them, and the quests to bring.

When to run each one · dashed line = where this guide stops (30)
Hall of ThanesNEW13–18The Deadmines17–21The Stockade22–26Blackfathom Deeps24–26Excavation SiteNEW26–28City of DalaranNEW30–35Gnomeregan29–38
1520253035

Quests, not trash

Dungeon kill XP is roughly a third of Classic; dungeon quest XP is about 2.3× Classic. Collect every quest before you go in and run each instance once.

Group finder

The finder lists groups but doesn't match or teleport you, and meeting stones don't summon. Five-player cap in every dungeon; five instance resets per hour.

Keep levels close

Each player's XP follows their own level, but anyone far above the mobs earns nothing. Keep the group within a few levels of each other.

For mates

Party board

Who in your group can run which dungeon right now, and who is pulling ahead or falling behind.

Add everyone you level with: name, class and level. The board shows which dungeons the whole group can run now, who is too low or too high for each, and when the group's levels are drifting apart. It's kept on this device; send your party code to your mates in your group chat and paste theirs in here, so everyone sees the same group.

Your group

Share with your mates

Your code is one short line. Post it in your group chat whenever you level, and paste everyone else's here. Pasting a code again updates that person's level.

Green: in the dungeon's level range. Amber: within two levels below it (fine with a strong group, or wait a level). Grey: above the range, so the trash gives that player little or no XP; the quests still pay. Ranges are the Forever ones used in this tab.

Profession guide

Professions

Which pair to take, where every Alliance trainer is, what to gather in each zone, and the camping system that ties it together.

Forever reworked professions more than any other levelling system: a dedicated Professions window and reagent bag, Junior gathering trainers in every starting zone, healing potions moved from Alchemy to First Aid, over 900 new recipes, the Merchant's Favor crate economy, and Camping, which gives every profession a one-hour buff object at skill 20. Skill caps still follow Classic: Journeyman at skill 50 / level 10, Expert at 125 / level 20, Artisan at 35. Verified in beta

Which pair

GoalPickWhy
Fastest levellingSkinning + Herbalism (or Mining) · First Aid + Cooking from day oneNo detours; gathering is learnable at level 1; First Aid now makes healing potions; Cooking gives +5% kill XP and the campfire. Legacy: Well Rested, Gourmand, Field Guide
Early gold on a fresh economyHerbalism + Skinning, or Herbalism + MiningNo live prices yet. Historically liquid at launch: Linen, Light Leather and Hide, Copper/Tin/Silver bars, Peacebloom, Briarthorn, Bruiseweed, Mageroyal, Stranglekelp, Swiftthistle, Small Lustrous Pearl. Forever signals: potion herbs are now consumed by First Aid; bags; necklace enchants; camp mats (Light Leather, Simple Wood); Waylaid Crates; Scarce mats. Riding at 40 (100 g) is the sink. Don't craft wands to vendor
Self-sufficiencyCloth → Tailoring + Enchanting · Leather/mail → Skinning + Leatherworking · Plate → Mining + Blacksmithing · Utility → Mining + Engineering · Casters/healers → Herbalism + AlchemyOwn bags by 12–15; armor kits and the Camp Tent at skill 20; Reagent Bot in the field; Swiftness and mana potions
By classMage/Priest/Warlock → Tailoring + Enchanting · Rogue/Druid → Skinning + LW · Hunter → Skinning + LW or Mining + Eng · Warrior/Paladin → Mining + BS (Crusader's Boots at 85) or Mining + Eng · Paladin healer → Herbalism + AlchemyMatches the Forever guide consensus

Camp objects are per player, so spread professions across your regular group: Cooking + Leatherworking + Fishing + Skinning between four people means campfire, Camp Tent, Fish Bowl and Camp Chair every hour for everyone.

Camping: what each profession adds at skill 20

Build the fire (Cooking 1), sit at it for about a minute, take the buffs. All of your objects share a one-hour cooldown; buffs don't stack with the matching class buff. Outdoors only, not inside cities and not too close to another camp (one source). The intro quests (The Great Outdoors in every start, then Camping 101 for your profession) teach the object.

Merchant's Favor

Waylaid Crates planner

Which crates you can fill from what you already gather or make, what each pays in Favor, and where to hand them in.

A plain Waylaid Crate drops from mobs in the world. Right-click it to read the label and it turns into one of 30 typed crates, such as Waylaid Crate: Apprentice Ore. You don't choose the type. Fill it with one of the bundles it lists, right-click to seal it, and hand the sealed crate to Marcy Baker at Three Corners in Redridge for Merchant's Favor, the currency for the Commerce Authority's recipes. Verified in beta

Tell the planner what you gather or make and your level. It shows every crate you can fill from that, what each pays, and the cheapest bundle. If you've just looted a crate, pick it from the list underneath to see whether to fill it, hold it or sell it.

What do you gather or make?

Just looted a crate?

What a crate pays

Raw crates (Herbs, Ore, Textiles, Curiosities) pay 5, 10 or 15 Favor at Apprentice, Journeyman and Expert. Crafted crates (Fabrics, Ingots, Parts) always pay double: 10, 20 or 30. The label decides which you get, not luck. Verified in beta

Your first sealed crate, or your first Craftsman's Writ, also gives a Shipping Label: 50 Favor, 2,000 Commerce Authority rep and 660 XP, once per character. The Legacy perk Performance Bonus gives a 15% chance at max rank to double a crate's Favor.

Where to hand them in

Marcy Baker, Supply Officer, Three Corners, Redridge 9.7, 70.9. The camp is the crossroads just inside Redridge where the Goldshire, Lakeshire and Darkshire roads meet. It has its own auctioneer (Quickcoin, 9.7, 72.0) for buying empty crates and missing mats on the spot. Verified in beta

  • Elwynn: road east from Goldshire through Eastvale.
  • Dun Morogh: tram to Stormwind, then the Elwynn road.
  • Teldrassil: Auberdine ship to Stormwind Harbor, then the road.
  • Zephras: Dalaran portal to the Mage Tower, then the road.
  • From 18–20: fly to Lakeshire and ride west.

No other Alliance turn-in point exists in any source.

Rules worth knowing

  • Apprentice and Journeyman crates need level 10, Expert 20, Artisan 35.
  • Empty crates trade; sealed ones are soulbound. Mail an empty crate to the alt who has the mats before you fill it.
  • Every recipe up to skill 150 costs 30 or 45 Favor and needs no reputation, so rep hardly matters at 1–30.
  • Turn-ins pay little silver. Early on the mats can be worth more on the auction house: one beta tester's 20 Strange Dust paid 4s 80c as a crate against 47s listed. Unverified

Weapon atlas · 05 Druid

Your weapon finally matters in forms.

In Forever, a druid's auto-attack in Cat, Bear and Dire Bear Form deals the same damage per second as the weapon you have equipped, at a fixed speed: 1.0 seconds in Cat Form and 2.5 in Bear Form. Abilities that deal weapon damage, such as Claw, use the same numbers, and enchants, procs and weightstones now work in forms. So feral picks go by the weapon's DPS, and a weapon's own speed doesn't matter. Balance picks go by spell power and Restoration by healing. [27][59][60]

Druids can use staves, two-handed and one-handed maces, daggers and fist weapons, plus held-in-off-hand items. Night Elves start with staves and daggers, so train Two-Handed Maces with Buliwyf Stonehand in Ironforge before your first mace upgrade. Darnassus (Ilyenia Moonfire) teaches staves, daggers and fist weapons; Stormwind (Woo Ping) staves and daggers. Skyborne druids can use maces from level 1. [57][61]

D Drop

Nothing worth chasing for your class here at 1–30. Wear what drops, or buy a cheap green on the auction house.

No plate before 40. Warriors and Paladins wear mail until they learn Plate Mail at 40, so the mail picks here are theirs. Hunters and Shaman wear leather until they learn Mail at 40: mail can't be equipped before then.

Some armour shares a quest with a weapon-atlas pick, so it's one or the other: Blackfathom Villainy gives Gravestone Scepter or Arctic Buckler, Dark Ritual Leggings or Cultist's Armguards; Prehistoric Prism gives Heavehammer or Explorer's League Dustcover.

Stats are from late-beta data (22 Oct). Between early and late October Blizzard cut 26 quest rewards from blue to green, including every Hall of Thanes reward. Check the tooltip before you choose on launch day.

Crafted blues from Merchant's Favor patterns (Tailoring, Leatherworking and Blacksmithing sets) are Bind on Pickup: only the crafter can wear them. BoE world drops and vendor greens aren't listed; buy one on the auction house only to fill an empty slot.

Sources: EverGear item data (22 Oct) · AllTheThings Forever database · ForeverLoot (Wowhead and wowtbc.gg, 4 Oct) · ForeverItemFinder (1 Nov build) · method.gg Forever dungeons · kami-labs Gnomeregan drops. Labels: unmarked cards are confirmed by two or more Forever datasets; Classic data is a Classic item Forever didn't change; Unverified has one source.

            Buy for professions

            Good value right now

              Buy list from the latest scan

              Don't buy in launch week

              Unless it is a bottleneck you can't farm. Gold is scarce and everything is overpriced for the first few days.

              Buy starter mats in weeks 2–4

              Linen, Light Leather and Copper fall as the levelling wave moves on. Camping objects and Waylaid Crates stop them crashing to nothing.

              Farm or buy First Aid herbs early

              Briarthorn and Bruiseweed don't get the usual starter-herb crash, because every class now makes healing potions from them.

              Never beat the vendor

              Threads, vials, spices, flux and Simple Wood are sold by vendors. An AH listing above that price is a trap.

              Cap Scarce mats at the Black Market price

              Mister Graphed at Powderfuse Port sells Pyrite, Pristine Leather and Frilled Lichen for 5 g (4.5 g with Bartering), once you can reach him.

              Recipes are lottery tickets

              Patterns and camp blueprints swung from +500% to −90% on beta. Buy them cheap and relist; never vendor one without checking.

                Profession cost

                What a profession costs to level

                Pick a profession and a skill target. The list nets out the intermediates you make yourself (bolts, grinding stones, powders) and prices the rest at today's reference price. A level 30 character can train to 225, so that is the top target.

                MaterialQtyEachCostGet it fromAdd to list

                Routes come from the Forever beta guides at wow-professions.com and foreverchanges.pro. Recipes turn grey about 25 points earlier than in Classic, so Classic routes overshoot. Counts may change at launch.

                Shopping list

                Your shopping list

                Tap + beside any material in the profession cost table or the watchlist, or add a whole route at once. The total uses today's reference prices, and vendor goods use the vendor's price. Copy it straight into Auctionator (Shopping tab → Import), where each line keeps your quantity and a price ceiling of 25% over the usual price.

                Price alerts

                Tell me when a price crosses a line

                The twice-daily price check watches the alerts below and sends a notification to your phone when one crosses its line. A below alert watches the cheapest listing (a chance to buy). An above alert watches the median (a chance to sell). Each fires once per crossing, then re-arms when the price goes back. Alerts only start after launch, once real prices arrive.

                Add an alert

                New alerts are checked on this device straight away. To get them on your phone, copy the request and send it to Claude in the WOW FOREVER project; the twice-daily check picks them up from then on.

                Watchlist

                Every material the guide uses

                ItemCheapestMedianvs 7 daysListedSignalTrendList and alerts

                How this works

                Method, signals and limits

                Twice a day, at about 7:15 am and 7:15 pm AEDT, a scheduled task reads the AHledger data for this auction house, updates the prices and their history, and rewrites the notes at the top of this tab. Everything else on the page (signals, buy list, profession costs) is worked out from those prices when you open it.

                SignalRule the page usesWhat to do
                ▲ RisingMedian at least 15% above its 7-day median (25% in launch fortnight)Sell what you hold; don't buy unless you must
                ▼ FallingMedian at least 15% below its 7-day median (25% in launch fortnight)Wait if you are buying; sell now if you are holding
                Good buyCheapest listing 20% or more under the reference price (30% at launch), with 20+ unitsBuy what your route needs
                Great buyCheapest listing 35% or more under the reference (45% at launch)Buy your full shopping list
                OverpricedCheapest listing 30% over the reference, or above the vendor's priceFarm it, or buy from the vendor
                ThinUnder 20 units or under 3 sellersOne seller sets this price; treat it with care

                The reference price is the 7-day median when there is one, then the 30-day median, then today's median. Prices older than 24 hours lose their buy and sell verdicts; older than 72 hours, no signals are shown at all. For the first fortnight after launch (to 19 Nov) medians are unreliable, so the thresholds are wider.

                What the data covers

                • One house: PvP, Alliance, the one the Oceanic and US servers share. Forever has no realms and AHledger has no separate Oceanic market: players and stress-test listings show Oceanic and US characters on the same house, so AHledger's "PvP Alliance US" market is ours. Blizzard hasn't confirmed this in writing. Gold can't move between houses, so other houses' prices are context only.
                • Until the AHledger API is allowed in Claude's settings, each update reads the public market page, which lists the top 100 items by quantity. Materials outside that list keep their last known price and are shown as older.
                • Prices are player addon scans uploaded to AHledger, not Blizzard data. A scan is a snapshot: some listings will already have sold.

                  Compiled by Claude · Edition 09 Nov 2026. Sources are listed in the Levelling guide tab.
                  Addons

                  Addons for Forever

                  Which addons have Forever builds, what each one does on screen, and the Classic favourites to leave behind. Four tiers, from the seven to install before you log in to the comfort extras.

                  How Forever addons work. Forever runs on the modern (Midnight-era) client, not the Classic one, so a Classic addon does not load: only files built for Forever do. Install into World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns (the CurseForge app does this if you select Forever as the game). Where an author ships a separate Forever file its name ends in -forever; otherwise filter by game version 1.60.1. Addons that call themselves out of date usually declare the wrong client in their .toc. In combat, Blizzard hides buff, cooldown, threat and enemy-spell values from addons: they may display them, not read them to make decisions. That is why WeakAuras and the combat-log addons are gone and why the game ships its own damage meter and Cooldown Manager.

                  Status and versions were checked 20 Oct – 9 Nov 2026 across four independent trackers (listed under Sources). Files move daily in launch week: when in doubt, open the addon's Files tab on CurseForge and take the newest Forever entry. Forever-only Official Forever file Works on Forever Partial No Forever build

                  Tier 1

                  Install these first

                  The seven that make the 1–30 guide usable in game: the all-in-one companion, quest markers, coordinates for the pins, bags, and the auction house.

                  OneForAll top pick

                  The all-in-one Forever companion
                  Forever-only6.2.1, 8 Nov

                  The most-downloaded Forever addon (about 750,000 by 8 Nov) and the one to install first. /ofa or its minimap button opens one window with: a gear planner showing upgrades by slot for your spec; dungeon maps, boss loot with drop chances and every dungeon quest chain, with a popup showing who in your group can take them; all profession recipes, the nearest trainer and a Merchant's Favor guide; Library Books by status with nearby alerts; map extras (fog removed, zone level ranges, flight masters, boat and tram routes, flight times); a talent calculator for every class that imports talentsforever.com builds; and Forever's hunter pet abilities. Quality-of-life switches (auto loot, repair, sell junk, quest XP on the XP bar) are all off until you turn them on.

                  It covers most of what Books on Map, Zone Info, Dungeon Journal and GearQuest do, so you can skip those. Keep Questie for quest markers: OneForAll hides its own quest icons while Questie is loaded. Forever data is still filling in, so the odd quest or drop may be missing.

                  CurseForge

                  Questie install first

                  Quest givers and objectives on the map
                  Official Forever file12.3.1, 26 Oct

                  Puts every quest giver, objective area and turn-in on your map and minimap, and tracks what you've picked up. In Forever the point is the new quests: Questie's team ships a Forever file and reports new Forever quests back through its companion QuestieTrace, so coverage of the 1,000-odd new quests fills in week by week.

                  A missing marker on a new Forever quest means the data isn't in yet, not that you installed it wrong. Remove any unofficial "Questie Forever" upload; it wasn't made by the Questie team.

                  CurseForge · GitHub releases

                  Leatrix Plus install first

                  Quality-of-life switches in one panel
                  Official Forever file1.60.25-forever, 21 Oct

                  One settings panel (/ltp) of small comforts: auto-sell greys, auto-repair, faster looting, bigger quest log, hide the gryphons, dismount on cast, and so on. Each switch is independent, so turn on only what you want.

                  Take the file whose name ends in -forever. A few Classic options are missing on Forever; some switches need a /reload.

                  Leatrix Maps install first

                  A clearer, fully revealed world map
                  Official Forever file1.60.24-forever, 20 Oct

                  Reveals unexplored areas on the world map, adds coordinates under your cursor, and lets you shrink and move the map. The pins in this guide are zone coordinates, so this (or TomTom) is how you find them in game.

                  Pick one map addon: Leatrix Maps conflicts with OpenMap, Mapster and Magnify.

                  TomTom install first

                  Waypoint arrow to a coordinate
                  Official Forever filev4.3.13, 24 Oct

                  Type /way 42.5 71.7 and an arrow on screen points the way, with the distance. The quickest way to use the coordinates in this guide's hub cards.

                  Bagnon or Baganator install first

                  All your bags in one window
                  Official Forever fileBagnon 12.1.7 · Baganator 838, 18 Oct

                  Merges your bags into one searchable window and can show what your other characters are carrying or have banked, which matters once you're shuffling materials between alts for professions and Waylaid Crates.

                  Pick one. Baganator needs its Syndicator library (CurseForge installs it for you).

                  Auctionator install first

                  Auction house search, prices and posting
                  Official Forever file341, 13 Oct

                  Shopping lists you can rescan in one click, auction prices in item tooltips, and one-click posting that undercuts the lowest listing. Keeps separate price data per Forever house (PvE/PvP/HC/RP).

                  TradeSkillMaster has no Forever build, so this is the AH addon. Pair it with the Auction House tab here for the bigger picture.

                  Tier 2

                  Made for Forever's new systems

                  Forever changed training, professions, books, the sleeping bag and the auction house. These are the addons built around those changes.

                  AHledger

                  Price history in tooltips, deals and alerts
                  Forever-only

                  The addon behind the prices in this guide's Auction House tab. Scans the house (no more than every 15 minutes), then shows median, cheapest, 7-day change, listed count and sales speed in tooltips, plus recipe margins, a deals list and a watchlist with alerts. Uploading your scans with its sync app is what keeps the shared data fresh for everyone, including this guide.

                  Scans, deals and alerts are the useful parts. It doesn't post or buy for you; Blizzard blocks automated AH actions.

                  ahledger.com

                  What's Training?

                  Which spells your trainer has for you
                  Partialbeta 11.0.0

                  Adds a tab to your spellbook listing every spell and rank you can learn now, what each costs, and what comes at the next level. Useful in Forever because training costs changed on 2 Nov and new ranks no longer appear on your bars, so this is where you notice you've skipped one.

                  Forever support was only in a beta file at the last check. If it won't load, Nova Spell Rank Checker flags outdated ranks on your bars instead.

                  SkillUp Forever

                  Profession skill-up odds and routes
                  Forever-onlyv0.18.10-forever, 21 Oct

                  Shows, per recipe, how likely a craft is to give a skill point at your current skill, so you stop crafting a recipe the moment it goes grey. Forever's recipes grey out about 25 points earlier than Classic, which is exactly why this exists.

                  Books on Map Forever

                  Where the library books are
                  Forever-only2.0.4, 19 Oct

                  Marks the readable library books that give Forever's one-off rewards on the world map, and tracks which you've read. The alternative, HandyNotes: Forever Books, does the same on top of HandyNotes; use one.

                  ForeverSecrets

                  In-game guide to the Cozy Sleeping Bag chain
                  Forever-only

                  A small tracker that follows the seven steps of the Cozy Sleeping Bag chain (starts level 14, Westfall 37, 50), detects which step you're on from your quest log, and drops a map waypoint for the next one. More hidden chains are planned.

                  CurseForge

                  Zone Info: Forever

                  Zone level ranges in tooltips
                  Forever-only1.9.1, 18 Oct

                  Adds each zone's Forever level range to the map tooltip, so the datamined bands in this guide (Maestra's Post 19, Astranaar 20, Felfire Hill 29…) are there when you hover.

                  GearQuest Forever

                  Best quest and dungeon gear by slot
                  Forever-only Partialv1.0.2, 21 Oct

                  Lists the best available item for each slot at your level and class, where it comes from, and which quest gives it. A good companion to the Weapon atlas tab for the other slots.

                  Heavy (200–400 MB) and the data was still beta-incomplete. Install the core plus one class folder.

                  Tier 3

                  Dungeons and groups

                  Add these when you start running Hall of Thanes and the Deadmines. One boss mod, one threat meter.

                  Deadly Boss Mods

                  Boss timers and warnings
                  Official Forever file12.1.18, 26 Oct

                  Bars and shouts for boss abilities. In the 1–30 dungeons that means Hall of Thanes, Deadmines, Stockade, Blackfathom and the Excavation Site, as the DBM team adds each Forever encounter.

                  Early Forever files were labelled "Forever prep": check your dungeon actually has timers before you rely on them. BigWigs loads but had no Forever boss modules at the last check. Run one boss mod, not both.

                  ThreatClassic2 or Forever Meter

                  Threat meter
                  Official Forever file Forever-onlyTC2 2.75-forever · Forever Meter v1.14.0

                  A bar per party member showing who the mob will swing at next. Tanks watch it to hold aggro; damage dealers watch it to stop at about 90%. Forever Meter is the Forever-only option and can warn you aloud at a share you set (/fm warn 90).

                  Forever hides some combat values from addons, so threat shown in combat is Blizzard's figure, not the addon's own calculation. ThreatClassic2 has no healer mode.

                  Details! (or the built-in meter)

                  Damage and healing meter
                  Official Forever file16 Oct

                  Who did what in the last fight, by spell. Forever ships its own meter (damage, healing, interrupts, avoidable damage), so you only need Details! if you want per-spell breakdowns and chat reports.

                  On Forever, Details! shows Blizzard's numbers rather than computing its own. If its windows stay empty, switch to its alpha file. Skada and the original Recount don't load.

                  AtlasLoot Classic Forever

                  Dungeon loot tables
                  Forever-only Partial1.2.6, 20 Oct

                  Browse what each boss drops before you run, with per-class best-in-slot by phase. Needs its FojjiCore library.

                  Lists items players have already seen, so the 1–30 dungeons fill in during launch week. Choose this project over the other AtlasLoot uploads.

                  Dungeon Journal

                  Retail-style journal for Forever dungeons
                  Forever-only Partial1.6.5, 19 Oct

                  /dj opens a journal with each dungeon's bosses, abilities and loot, and tells you which dungeon quests you still have to collect and at what level they unlock. Pairs with the Dungeons tab here.

                  Loot above level 30 was incomplete at the last check.

                  Decursive

                  One-click dispels for healers
                  Official Forever file2.9.0-RC3-forever, 4 Oct

                  Shows who in the party has a curable curse, poison, disease or magic effect and lets you clear it with a click. Priests, Paladins, Druids, Shamans.

                  Tier 4

                  Interface and comfort

                  Much of what used to need an addon is built into the Forever client. These fill the gaps.

                  Edit Mode (built in) or Bartender4

                  Move and resize your action bars
                  Works on Forever4.18.3.1, 2 Oct

                  Forever runs on the modern client, so Esc → Edit Mode already moves bars, frames and the minimap with grids and profiles. Bartender4 is for people who want more bars, paging and the gryphons gone.

                  Bartender4 uses its Retail file; no Forever file needed.

                  Cooldown Manager (built in)

                  Blizzard's own cooldown and buff tracker
                  Works on ForeverCooldown Manager Centered v5.9.1

                  Off by default: Options → Gameplay Enhancement. Gathers your key cooldowns and procs into one movable cluster. It covers most of what people used WeakAuras for, and it is the only thing that can read your buffs reliably in combat (see below). Cooldown Manager Centered makes it easier to read.

                  BasicMinimap

                  Square, movable minimap
                  Works on Foreverv12.1.4, 20 Oct

                  Replaces SexyMap, which has no Forever file. Square minimap, hide the clutter, group the addon buttons.

                  Run one minimap replacement only.

                  BugSack + BugGrabber

                  Catch addon errors quietly
                  Works on Forever12.1.7

                  Launch week will have half-ported addons. These two catch their Lua errors in a sack you open later, instead of a red box in the middle of a pull. Install them first and you'll know which addon to blame.

                  ForeverMail

                  Mail that understands first and last names
                  Forever-only

                  Postal is Retail-only, and Forever characters have two names. ForeverMail is the Postal replacement that auto-completes them and opens all your mail at once.

                  Delete Cheapest Item

                  Free a slot when your bags are full
                  Works on Foreverv1.4.0, 14 Oct

                  When loot won't fit, one command deletes the cheapest grey in your bags. Saves a vendor trip in the middle of a Westfall field.

                  Armory

                  Character armory

                  Look up your character and your mates on the WoW Forever armory: gear, talents, gear score and a 3D model.

                  armorywowforever.com

                  Your heroes, on the Forever armory

                  Gear, talents, gear score and a 3D model for any Forever character, read from Blizzard's own character data. It covers the Americas and Europe megaservers; Oceanic characters should show under the Americas.

                  Open the armory ↗ Opens in a new tab
                  Look up a hero

                  Find a character

                  Forever names have a first and a last name, and the armory searches by both. Fill them in here, then open the armory: the name is copied, so you only have to paste it into the armory's search.

                  Copy name and open the armory ↗

                  Your crew

                  Everyone on your Party board

                  The characters from the Party board and your own character setup, ready to look up. Use full first and last names on the board so the armory search finds them.

                  What it shows

                  On each character page

                  Gear, slot by slot

                  Every equipped item with its gems, enchants and set bonuses, so you can see exactly what a mate is wearing before you pass on a drop.

                  The character in 3D

                  A turnable model of the hero in their current gear, built from Wowhead's model viewer.

                  Talents and dual spec

                  Both talent builds side by side, including Forever's new talents.

                  Gearscore and the leaderboard

                  A single gear score per character, and a leaderboard you can filter by region.

                  Talent calculator

                  Plan a build for any of the nine classes before you spend the points, in eight languages.

                  Guilds

                  Search a guild as well as a character, once your crew has one.

                  Why it opens in a new tab. This guide can't show another website inside it or read live character data, so the armory opens on its own. The armory is a community site built on Blizzard's character data, not a Blizzard page.
